candidates.name: PostgreSQL + pgvector
candidates.role: Portable authoritative source/Claim/Evidence registry and exact metrics, with full-text and vector retrieval.

evidence.claim: pgvector provides exact and approximate vector search, HNSW/IVFFlat, filtering and hybrid-search examples; PostgreSQL GIN is a preferred full-text index.

limitations: Approximate vector indexes can reduce recall or filtered result counts; compare against exact search on the target workload.
Horizontal scale and ANN filtering may need tuning or a separate retrieval service at higher load.
candidates.reason: Relational-first category leader; joins exact numeric facts, source references, ACL filters, lexical search and vectors with low index drift. Self-host TCO remains unmeasured, so economics is neutral. Weighted expert prior 81/100.

candidates.name: Supabase Postgres + pgvector
candidates.role: Managed PostgreSQL vector/FTS service with Supabase Auth and Row Level Security.

evidence.claim: Supabase documents pgvector storage, SQL RPC for vector operators, keyword+dense hybrid retrieval with RRF, and database-enforced RLS.

limitations: Requires a Supabase account and project; no existing account or region is assumed.
Vector RPC and policies add product-specific integration and security configuration.
candidates.reason: Lower-operations managed alternative to generic PostgreSQL; provider coupling and unpriced workload keep it below the portable category leader. Weighted expert prior 79/100.

candidates.name: Neo4j Aura
candidates.role: Rebuildable derived property-graph projection for multi-hop hardware, kernel, recipe, Claim and Evidence retrieval; PostgreSQL remains the authoritative ledger.

evidence.claim: Neo4j provides graph traversal plus full-text and approximate vector search indexes; official docs recommend ranking independent lexical and vector results before combining them.

limitations: Search syntax and filtering capabilities vary by Neo4j version and Aura tier.
This projection and its ACL fields are not authoritative for facts, typed legality or authorization; validate against PostgreSQL and deterministic rules.
candidates.reason: Property-graph projection leader over Neptune Database for the provider-unspecified scenario; source facts and ACL authority stay in PostgreSQL. Weighted expert prior 80/100.

candidates.name: Amazon Neptune Database
candidates.role: Managed AWS graph projection candidate for RDF/SPARQL and property-graph Gremlin/openCypher retrieval; canonical Claim/Evidence/ACL ledger remains outside.

evidence.claim: Neptune Database supports SPARQL 1.1 and property-graph query languages on managed graph infrastructure.

limitations: VPC, IAM, AWS data plane and service-specific query semantics increase cloud coupling.
Separate Neptune Database and Neptune Analytics documentation must be checked before assigning features.
candidates.reason: Good managed graph/RDF candidate when AWS is selected; held below Neo4j Aura until provider and graph-model requirements are known. Weighted expert prior 75/100.

candidates.name: Amazon Neptune Analytics
candidates.role: Separate memory-optimized graph analytics and vector-in-traversal service for exploration.

evidence.claim: Neptune Analytics can load graphs from Neptune Database or S3 and supports analytics, graph queries and vector similarity.

limitations: It complements rather than replaces Neptune Database for a mutable application graph.
A graph has one vector index with a fixed dimension at creation; embedding updates are not ACID/atomic.
candidates.reason: Useful optional analytical companion, not a primary DSE KG store; assessed only in the graph-analytics role. Weighted expert prior 63/100.

candidates.name: Stardog Cloud
candidates.role: Managed RDF projection and SPARQL/reasoning/SHACL validation plane over the canonical Claim/Evidence ledger.

evidence.claim: Stardog documents SPARQL 1.1, query-time OWL/rule reasoning, SHACL constraints and a fully managed cloud offering.

limitations: License, cloud region, cost, service boundary and exact supported SHACL profile need vendor confirmation.
Dense retrieval may require a separate derived vector index.
candidates.reason: RDF/SHACL category leader for legality-first DSE knowledge; higher proprietary and unknown-cost risk than self-managed Jena. Weighted expert prior 87/100.

candidates.name: Apache Jena Fuseki + TDB2
candidates.role: Portable self-managed RDF/SPARQL projection with persistent triple store and SHACL validation over the canonical Claim/Evidence ledger.

evidence.claim: Jena documents Fuseki HTTP SPARQL service, TDB2 persistent storage, and SHACL Core/SPARQL constraint processing.

limitations: The team owns deployment, upgrades, backups, HA, security and capacity planning.
Managed operation requires a separate hosting decision.
candidates.reason: Strong open, portable option when operations ownership is acceptable; category runner-up to managed Stardog Cloud. Self-host TCO is unmeasured, so economics is neutral. Weighted expert prior 78/100.

candidates.name: Qdrant
candidates.role: Vector-first derived retrieval index for dense/sparse candidates, payload filters and multi-stage reranking.

evidence.claim: Qdrant documents prefetch/multi-stage hybrid search, payload-based tenant filtering and tiered multitenancy.

limitations: It is not a knowledge graph or ontology/SHACL validator.
Full-text support is intentionally narrower than general lexical search engines.
candidates.reason: Vector category leader for provider-neutral hybrid candidate generation and many-session tenant filtering. Cloud/self-host TCO is unmeasured, so economics is neutral. Weighted expert prior 80/100.

candidates.name: Weaviate
candidates.role: Vector database with built-in BM25/vector hybrid, property filters and configurable fusion.

evidence.claim: Weaviate hybrid queries combine BM25F and vector result sets with a configurable fusion method and relative weights.

limitations: Do not treat object references as the authoritative typed hardware legality model without separate validation.
Cloud and self-managed behavior should be checked at the pinned release.
candidates.reason: Convenient hybrid vector option with usable metadata filters; category second behind Qdrant on portability and source-role separation. Weighted expert prior 74/100.

candidates.name: Milvus
candidates.role: Vector database for dense/sparse multi-vector search, scalar filtering and reranking.

evidence.claim: Milvus documents dense/sparse hybrid candidates, RRF or weighted rankers, and both pre-filtered and iterative-filtered ANN search.

limitations: Complex filtering can increase search latency.
Deployment, consistency level, storage and managed Zilliz Cloud features need separate review.
candidates.reason: Strong vector/scale feature set but higher operational burden in self-managed form; category third. Self-host TCO is unmeasured, so economics is neutral. Weighted expert prior 68/100.

candidates.name: Pinecone
candidates.role: Fully managed vector search with namespaces, metadata filters and sparse/dense hybrid options.

evidence.claim: Pinecone documents managed vector indexes, namespace partitioning, metadata filters and sparse/dense search.

limitations: Provider coupling and region choices require explicit review.
Usage-based cost cannot be estimated without corpus, query and retention volumes; metadata namespaces are not a substitute for authorization design.
candidates.reason: Highest managed convenience but weakest portability and unpriced scale uncertainty in this vector category. Weighted expert prior 67/100.

candidates.name: Vespa
candidates.role: Search/ranking platform for configurable BM25, nearest-neighbor retrieval, ranking profiles and reranking.

evidence.claim: Vespa supports sparse and dense top-k retrieval with configurable ranking phases, including RRF examples and later reranking.

limitations: Schema and rank-profile design create a steeper learning and operations curve.
No workload benchmark exists to justify its extra ranking flexibility yet.
candidates.reason: Hybrid-search category leader when ranking flexibility is a central experimental requirement; not the simplest first deployment. Weighted expert prior 81/100.

candidates.name: OpenSearch
candidates.role: Portable lexical/vector search engine with hybrid queries and score- or rank-based combination.

evidence.claim: OpenSearch combines keyword and semantic queries using normalization or RRF and documents efficient ANN filtering.

limitations: RRF and filtering support depend on engine/version; managed-service feature parity must be checked.
It is redundant with Elastic or Vespa as the same lexical/vector serving plane.
candidates.reason: Good open hybrid baseline with portability and RRF; category second behind Vespa's ranking flexibility. Managed/self-host TCO is unmeasured, so economics is neutral. Weighted expert prior 77/100.

candidates.name: Elasticsearch / Elastic Cloud
candidates.role: Managed or self-managed BM25 and vector search with hybrid RRF retrieval.

evidence.claim: Elastic documents full-text+vector hybrid search and recommends RRF to combine result ranks.

limitations: Elastic Cloud, serverless and self-managed tiers can differ in features and commercial terms.
Avoid pairing with OpenSearch unless a measured migration or product boundary warrants both.
candidates.reason: Capable managed hybrid search but product/edition and commercial dependencies reduce fit while provider requirements are open. Weighted expert prior 74/100.

candidates.name: Versioned object storage + Parquet/Iceberg
candidates.role: Canonical, immutable/versioned storage for raw sources, traces, run manifests and analytical tables.

evidence.claim: S3 Versioning preserves object versions, S3 Object Lock protects versions under retention, and Iceberg records snapshots for time travel and branch/tag lifecycle.

limitations: Object/table formats do not provide graph, lexical or vector retrieval on their own.
Snapshot retention and object versions increase storage costs; provider-neutral object-store feature parity needs checking.
candidates.reason: Strong evidence-lake role and format portability; no within-category competitor is scored because storage is its own required role. Retention, query and egress TCO are unmeasured, so economics is neutral. Weighted expert prior 85/100.

candidates.name: ClickHouse
candidates.role: Columnar SQL serving/analytics layer for repeated aggregation of run and event metric tables.

evidence.claim: ClickHouse can query Iceberg tables in object storage and load selected data into MergeTree tables for repeated analytical queries.

limitations: It is not the graph legality or claim-provenance authority.
A serving copy duplicates data and adds freshness/reconciliation work; validate only if PostgreSQL/Iceberg aggregate workloads require it.
candidates.reason: Useful optional metric serving plane; compare only against columnar analytics alternatives, not against the evidence lake. Weighted expert prior 78/100.

candidates.name: Microsoft GraphRAG
candidates.role: Optional indexing/retrieval framework for community summaries and whole-corpus/global questions.

evidence.claim: GraphRAG extracts entities, relationships and claims, builds communities and multi-level summaries, then offers global, local, DRIFT and basic search.

limitations: Global search and index generation can be resource-intensive.
Generated communities/reports are derived summaries; exact metrics and source truth must come from structured evidence.
candidates.reason: Best considered for demonstrated whole-corpus question classes; it is not a database and is not ranked against storage candidates. Weighted expert prior 69/100.

candidates.name: LightRAG
candidates.role: Optional graph/vector RAG framework emphasizing local/global retrieval and incremental updates.

evidence.claim: The project documents incremental update/selective deletion and multiple graph/vector/KV storage backends; its rebuild tool treats graph/KV data as authoritative over vector indexes.

limitations: Project documentation says default local persistence is for small-scale testing/evaluation, not production.
Graph/vector multi-write drift, deletion behavior and embedding-model changes require consistency checks and rebuild procedures.
candidates.reason: Potential dynamic local/multihop retrieval framework; backend consistency and fast-changing project API lower confidence. Runtime and LLM-call TCO are unmeasured, so economics is neutral. Weighted expert prior 71/100.
